title: Research Engine Mostly-Local EXTRACT Redesign v1
goal: Return to first principles on research-engine EXTRACT and identify, benchmark, and if justified implement a provenance-preserving mostly-local extraction architecture that makes STANDARD Codex a rare ambiguity/failure fallback rather than the default, while reusing accepted local document/VERIFY infrastructure and not repeating approaches already invalidated by durable evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A current literature and implementation survey identifies how comparable local scientific-document, structured-information-extraction, evidence-grounding, claim-extraction, and high-precision fallback systems solve the same or adjacent problem.

Previously failed approaches are explicitly excluded from reconsideration unless new evidence changes the failed premise; in particular, the already-tested Qwen3.5-4B grounded-candidate EXTRACT architecture is not simply rerun with cosmetic prompt changes.

The design reuses accepted production assets where they help: authoritative-PDF provenance, paper-package/document sidecars, native+structured parsing, CodeFormulaV2, table escalation, the local inference broker, and bounded Qwen VERIFY.

At least three materially distinct mostly-local EXTRACT architectures are compared on expected semantic quality, provenance preservation, local resource cost, implementation complexity, and likely Codex-fallback rate.

The selected architecture is evidence-first and fail-closed: every accepted extracted claim remains traceable to authoritative PDF page/region/text evidence, and low-confidence/disputed cases fall through to STANDARD Codex rather than being silently accepted.

A benchmark plan evaluates claim-level precision/recall or agreement, page/type agreement, evidence grounding, hallucination/unsupported-claim rate, local latency/VRAM/RAM, and empirical Codex fallback fraction on preserved production-like jobs.

The primary local path is runnable on the current Lambda host with dual RTX A4500 GPUs, using quantization/CPU offload or model specialization where justified; hosted APIs are not introduced into the primary local path.
A candidate is promoted only if it materially reduces Codex EXTRACT usage while preserving a predeclared semantic-quality floor and authoritative provenance.

Production routing, if eventually changed, retains Codex STANDARD as a rare fallback. The already-accepted bounded page-scoped Qwen VERIFY route remains the known-good post-materialization safety baseline; this task may measure whether the new EXTRACT architecture makes parts of VERIFY redundant or complementary, but any production simplification/change requires an explicit later validation gate with the current route preserved as rollback.
The task records both successful and rejected architectural families so future work does not repeat failed bakeoffs.

ExtractBench 2026 evaluates value accuracy, completeness and source grounding across 370 documents / 4,869 pages; its public baseline ranks agentic extraction above one-shot self-hosted models, supporting architecture/harness work rather than another blind model swap.

LlamaIndex Extract v2.5 reports a purpose-built extraction agent harness with structural reasoning over document representations, intermediate representations, source-return tools, cross-page inspection, citations and confidence-gated review.
Google LangExtract demonstrates a local-compatible chunk/parallel/multipass extraction architecture with deterministic mapping of extracted values back to exact source character spans.

GLiNER2/2.5 provides compact schema-driven encoder IE; current GLiNER2.5 base is 194M and supports entities, classification, records/relations and constrained joint IE, making it a candidate span/type/relationship detector rather than a complete open-ended claim generator.

NuExtract3 explicitly separates verbatim-string extraction from abstractive string fields, matching raw_source_form versus normalized_form semantics, but ExtractBench reports weak one-shot value F1 relative to agentic systems; use only as a bounded component candidate.

Lift is a self-hosted schema-constrained document extractor with local HF/vLLM modes and materially stronger public extraction scores than NuExtract3, but its weights use a modified OpenRAIL-M license and its local path lacks the hosted verification/citation layer; benchmark/review before any promotion.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is a materially stronger 35B-total/3B-active MoE candidate for a hard-case local agent, but official serving recipes target newer/larger hardware than the Lambda A4500s; quantized feasibility must be proven before download.

SciFact decomposes scientific fact checking into retrieval/rationale selection and label prediction, and publishes citation-context to atomic-claim generation data; MultiVerS provides local scientific claim-verification checkpoints.

Recent clinical IE distillation work reports small BioBERT students trained from LLM teacher labels approaching teacher performance with much lower inference cost, supporting a strategy where Codex fallback results become supervised data for the local pipeline.
GUIDEX and broader distillation literature support synthetic/guideline-driven domain adaptation rather than relying indefinitely on zero-shot general models.

Family A — modular scientific IE cascade: local retrieval/reranking -> GLiNER2.5/structured span candidates -> small local claim normalizer -> MultiVerS/NLI + deterministic quote/page guards -> Codex residual fallback.
Family B — specialized document extractor: targeted Lift 9B or NuExtract3 on retrieved page/region subsets -> deterministic source anchoring -> local verifier -> Codex residual fallback.

Family C — local tool-using extraction agent: stronger quantized local reasoner (candidate Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) operates over sidecar search/read/locate tools and must cite exact regions; verifier/guard decides acceptance; Codex only on unresolved units.

Preferred architecture is hierarchical hybrid D: cheap A first, specialized B only where helpful, local agent C only for hard residuals, Codex STANDARD last. This maximizes reuse of accepted infrastructure and allows empirical fallback-rate measurement at each tier.
